To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plasma concentrations of nearly all amino-acids in subjects with DS are significantly different from those of healthy control subjects.
the production of nitric oxide is increased in DS subjects with dementia.

plasma amino acids and plasma concentrations of neopterin were altered in subjects with Down syndrome (a genetic disorder associated with Alzheimer’s disease) and that these alterations were related to the development of dementia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hypothesis of a role for NO in AD and DS.
the pathogenesis of dementia in DS.
the hypothesis that the increased oxidative stress in DS is involved in the development of AD in this population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cit/Arg and the neopterin ratio are increased in DS subjects with dementia and that the neopterin concentrations correlated with the Cit/Arg ratios only in the group with prevalent dementia.
plasma amino acid and neopterin levels in DS subjects with dementia are related to the Cit/ Arg ratio.
DS subjects with AD have a disturbed metabolism of NO and that neopterin concentrations are related to the production of NO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
plasma levels of nitric-oxide-related amino acids and neopentir are related to the development of dementia in DS subjects.
the Cit/Arg and neopterin ratios are useful biomarkers for the assessment of oxidative stress in AD.
plasma concentrations of amino acids and neopertin in DS subjects are related to development of clinical dementia and to the Cit/ Arg ratio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cit/Arg and neopterin concentrations may serve as biomarkers of oxidative stress.
the plasma levels of amino acids and neoperin in subjects with DS are related to the presence of AD and that the plasma levels are different in DS compared with healthy controls.
plasma levels of amino acids and neopeptin can be used to predict the onset of dementia in subjects with DS.
